inicio.kicker: Cinema with AI program · course 3 of 6 · 8 lessons
inicio.titulo: Motion as code with an agent: the video that comes out of the terminal, the same every time
inicio.lead: HyperFrames and Remotion turn HTML and React into MP4. You ask the agent, check it in five frames, tie the piece to a DESIGN.md, add a local voice and captions, and deliver a 15 s opening in 16:9 and 9:16. Everything renders on your machine, with no credits.
inicio.capa_alt: Dark editing desk with a timeline monitor, a keyboard, and a closed clapperboard; the course title is on the left.
inicio.aulas_sub: From the mental model to rendering in both formats: determinism, HyperFrames, the request to the agent, the brand, Remotion, libraries, audio, and your own piece.

itens: People who already use Claude Code or Codex in the terminal and want video, openings, or motion without a graphic editor.
People who make video for a company or a course and need to repeat the same piece with other text, another color, or another format.
Devs who want to know when to choose HTML (HyperFrames) and when to choose React (Remotion).

blocos.t: What you'll be able to do
itens: Prove that your render is deterministic and find what breaks that.
Ask the agent for a composition with the RISE method and check it in five frames before the MP4.
Write the video's DESIGN.md and fail any off-brand color with one command.
Add narration and karaoke captions made on your machine and deliver checked 16:9 and 9:16 versions.
Linux or macOS with Node 22 or newer, FFmpeg, Python 3, and git. On Windows, use WSL.
About 2 GB free: the render browser (~240 MB), the local voice (~340 MB), and the transcription model (~490 MB) download on first use.
Recommended: course 0 (Direction) for the language of shots and light. Sound, editing, and ethics are in course 2.
